jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.name: Satoru Gojo
jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.summary: Gojo is a special grade sorcerer who is widely called the strongest of his era. He fights by controlling space itself: attacks slow down before they can reach him, and he can pull, push or erase anything in front of him.

abilities.name: Limitless: Infinity
abilities.what: Gojo's inherited technique puts an 'infinity' of space between him and anything coming at him, so attacks slow down and never actually touch him. Since his student days he keeps it switched on all the time and lets it decide automatically what to block.
abilities.note: Episode/chapter are the wiki's debut fields for Limitless/Infinity; Wikipedia's episode 7 summary describes the Infinity barrier being explained.

abilities.name: Cursed Technique Lapse: Blue
abilities.what: Blue boosts Limitless to create a point that pulls everything around it inward, like a small black hole. Gojo uses it to drag enemies together, crush them, or yank himself across short distances at high speed.
abilities.note: Numbers from the wiki's debut fields only (publication order).

abilities.name: Cursed Technique Reversal: Red
abilities.what: Red reverses Blue: by running positive energy from his reverse cursed technique through Limitless, Gojo creates a repelling blast that throws targets away. The wiki notes it has at least twice Blue's output.
abilities.note: Numbers from the wiki's debut fields only.

abilities.name: Hollow Technique: Purple
abilities.what: Gojo smashes Blue and Red together to create 'imaginary mass' and fires it forward. It erases everything in its path.
abilities.note: First shown (publication order) against Hanami at the Kyoto Goodwill Event. In story order he first creates it in the Gojo's Past flashback (Wikipedia, season 2 episode 28 summary: 'another first').

abilities.name: Six Eyes
abilities.what: These are rare eyes passed down in the Gojo clan. They let him see cursed energy in very fine detail, even through a blindfold. They also make his techniques so efficient that he wastes almost no cursed energy, which is why he can keep Limitless running.
abilities.note: Numbers from the wiki's debut fields only; Wikipedia's character article describes what the Six Eyes do.

abilities.name: Domain Expansion: Unlimited Void
abilities.what: Gojo traps opponents in his domain and floods their minds with endless information, so they cannot think or move. He and anyone he is touching are unaffected.

abilities.name: Reverse Cursed Technique
abilities.what: He turns cursed energy into positive energy that heals his body. Gojo learned it while near death in his first fight with Toji, and it also powers Red and keeps his brain fresh while Infinity runs nonstop.
abilities.note: This is Gojo's first use. The technique itself appears earlier with other characters.

abilities.name: Black Flash
abilities.what: When cursed energy hits within a millionth of a second of a punch, space distorts and the blow lands far harder than normal (the wiki gives it 2.5 times the power). Gojo is first shown landing one on Sukuna, knocking him out for a moment.
abilities.note: Manga only. No anime episode is cited.

limits.what: Infinity can be cancelled. A domain (expansion or amplification) can dismiss it, and so can cursed tools with special techniques. Toji's Inverted Spear of Heaven is one example.
Keeping Infinity running is tiring. As a student he wore himself out holding it for days, which Toji took advantage of. As an adult he keeps his brain fresh by using reverse cursed technique nonstop.

Civilians limit his domain. In Shibuya he could only risk a 0.2-second Unlimited Void because the crowd was trapped with him. Clearing the transfigured humans afterwards left him drained, and that was when the Prison Realm was used.
After each Domain Expansion his cursed technique burns out. Against Sukuna he had to repair it with reverse cursed technique each time, and he could not manage a sixth Unlimited Void.

beaten.how: In 2006 Toji ambushed the exhausted student Gojo right after he dropped Infinity, stabbed him and won their first fight. Gojo survived by awakening reverse cursed technique and killed Toji with Hollow Purple in the rematch.
beaten.where: Gojo's Past (Hidden Inventory) arc, chapters 70–72, episode 27; rematch chapter 75, episode 28

beaten.who: Kenjaku (in Suguru Geto's body), using the Prison Realm
beaten.how: Gojo was worn down by the 0.2-second domain and the transfigured humans. Seeing his dead friend Geto's face froze him long enough for the Prison Realm to seal him.
beaten.where: Shibuya Incident arc, chapters 90–91, episodes 33–34 (the seal completes in episode 34)

beaten.how: Their domains matched and Gojo came close to winning. Sukuna then used Mahoraga's adaptation as a model for a slash that cuts the space Gojo stands in, which bypassed Infinity and killed him.
beaten.where: Shinjuku Showdown arc, chapters 223–236 (Gojo dies in chapter 236); manga, no anime episode cited

notes: Anime episode numbers are series-wide: season 2 episode 1 = episode 25, so episode 28 = season 2 episode 4.
Chapter numbers are from the main Jujutsu Kaisen manga (not Jujutsu Kaisen 0).
For 'who can beat Gojo': Toji (first fight), Kenjaku's Prison Realm seal (Shibuya), and Sukuna in Shinjuku. Sukuna is the only one who defeats him in a straight fight that he does not survive.
Shinjuku material (Black Flash, domain burnout, the Sukuna result) had not been animated in any source checked, so episode is null.
jujutsu-kaisen-satoru-gojou.powersLine: Limitless (Infinity, Blue, Red and Hollow Purple), the Six Eyes, his Domain Expansion, Unlimited Void, and Reverse Cursed Technique

goku-son.name: Son Goku
goku-son.series: Dragon Ball (Dragon Ball, Z, Super; GT and Daima listed separately)
goku-son.summary: Goku is a Saiyan martial artist who lives for fighting stronger opponents and keeps pushing past his limits. He mixes hand-to-hand combat with energy blasts and a long line of power-up transformations.

abilities.name: Kamehameha
abilities.what: Goku cups his hands, gathers his ki and fires it as a beam. It is Master Roshi's technique, but young Goku copied it after seeing it only once.
abilities.note: Goku's first Kamehameha is in Dragon Ball episode 8, where Wikipedia's summary has him copying it 'on the first try'. The technique first appears in manga chapter 14 when Roshi uses it, but the chapter where Goku first fires it was not confirmed.

abilities.name: Kaio-ken
abilities.what: King Kai's technique multiplies Goku's power, speed and senses for a short time by flooding his body with ki. The higher the multiplier, the harder it is on his body.
abilities.chapterSeries: Dragon Ball manga (continuous numbering; DBZ ch. 32 in Viz)
abilities.note: Numbers from the Dragon Ball Wiki's debut fields.

abilities.name: Spirit Bomb
abilities.what: Goku raises his hands and gathers energy from living things around him into one huge sphere. It needs time to charge and a pure heart to control, so it works best when others give their energy willingly.
abilities.chapterSeries: Dragon Ball manga (continuous numbering; DBZ ch. 18 in Viz)
abilities.note: Numbers from the Dragon Ball Wiki's debut fields. Wikipedia confirms that Goku finishes Kid Buu with a Spirit Bomb.

abilities.name: Instant Transmission
abilities.what: Goku locks on to someone's ki and appears next to them at once, even across planets, taking along anyone touching him. He learned it from the people of planet Yardrat.
abilities.chapterSeries: Dragon Ball manga (continuous numbering; DBZ ch. 142 in Viz)
abilities.note: Numbers from the Dragon Ball Wiki; Wikipedia confirms where he learned it.

abilities.name: Flight (Bukū-jutsu)
abilities.what: By controlling his ki, Goku can fly on his own, so after training with Kami he stops relying on the Flying Nimbus.
abilities.note: No source gave a first-appearance number for Goku's flight.

forms.name: Great Ape (Ōzaru)
forms.what: When a tailed Saiyan looks at a full moon, he turns into a giant, rampaging ape.

forms.name: Kaio-ken
forms.what: A short burst that multiplies all his stats, at the cost of heavy strain on his body.

forms.name: Super Saiyan
forms.what: The legendary golden-haired transformation, set off by rage when Frieza kills Krillin.

forms.name: Super Saiyan 2
forms.arc: Majin Buu Saga (Babidi arc, vs. Majin Vegeta)
forms.what: A sharper, spikier step up from Super Saiyan with crackling lightning. Goku reveals it against Majin Vegeta.
forms.note: The form first appears with Gohan (manga chapter 408, DBZ episode 184). No source gave Goku's first chapter or episode in it.

forms.name: Super Saiyan 3
forms.what: Very long hair, no eyebrows and a huge jump in power, but it burns through his energy fast.

forms.name: Super Saiyan God
forms.arc: God of Destruction Beerus Saga (film: Battle of Gods, 2013)
forms.what: A slimmer, red-haired god form created by a ritual in which six Saiyans pour their power into him.
forms.note: Manga chapter from the Dragon Ball Wiki only.

forms.name: Super Saiyan Blue (Super Saiyan God Super Saiyan)
forms.what: Super Saiyan with god ki, blue hair and calm, tight control over his energy.
forms.note: Wikipedia's episode 25 summary has Goku explaining his 'new transformation' to Frieza. Episode 24 and chapter 5 come from the Dragon Ball Wiki.

forms.name: Super Saiyan Blue Kaio-ken
forms.what: Kaio-ken stacked on top of Super Saiyan Blue. Blue's control makes the combination survivable, but it is still risky.
forms.note: Manga chapter from the Dragon Ball Wiki only.

forms.name: Ultra Instinct Sign
forms.what: A divine state in which his body dodges and counters on its own without conscious thought. Its raw attack power is weaker than its defence.

forms.name: Mastered Ultra Instinct
forms.what: The completed Ultra Instinct, with silver hair. He both defends and attacks automatically.
forms.note: The Dragon Ball Wiki now calls this 'Perfected Ultra Instinct'. Goku also reaches it against Jiren in the manga, but the chapter number was not confirmed.

forms.name: True Ultra Instinct
forms.what: Goku's own version of Ultra Instinct, which lets him fight with his Saiyan emotions instead of the calm, emotionless state it normally needs.
forms.note: Manga only. Chapter from the Dragon Ball Wiki only.

forms.name: Golden Great Ape
forms.what: A golden Great Ape, which Goku reaches after regrowing his tail. He struggles to control it.

forms.name: Super Saiyan 4 (GT)
forms.what: Red fur, black hair and the power of the Golden Great Ape in a human-sized body. It also returns child Goku to adult size.
forms.note: The Dragon Ball Wiki lists 'Back in the Game' (episode 34) as the debut. Wikipedia's summaries show him fully in the form from episode 35 ('Goku's Ascension'), so he probably transforms at the end of 34.

forms.name: Super Saiyan 4 (Daima)
forms.what: A redesigned Super Saiyan 4 by Akira Toriyama that follows Super Saiyan 3. Neva unlocks it in Mini Goku, and in Daima Goku had already trained for it after Majin Buu.

limits.what: Kaio-ken strains his body. King Kai warns that pushing the multiplier too far makes it backfire, and after using Kaio-ken in Super Saiyan Blue against Hit, Goku could not control his ki for a while.
Super Saiyan 3 uses up energy very quickly. In a living body against Kid Buu, it drained him so badly that he could not recover his power.
Ultra Instinct wears out his body. Against Jiren and Kefla he could not keep the state up, and in the manga against Granolah it grew less accurate the longer he fought.
Instant Transmission needs a ki signature to lock on to. In the Cell Games Saga he could not reach New Namek because their ki was too far away to sense.

beaten.how: After a long, even final, both fighters were exhausted. Goku fainted mid-sentence while claiming the title, so Jackie Chun won.
beaten.where: 21st World Martial Arts Tournament final; manga chapter 53, Dragon Ball episode 28

beaten.how: Tien won the 22nd tournament final and Goku finished runner-up again. Toriyama says he deliberately had Goku lose the first two tournaments and win the third.
beaten.where: 22nd World Martial Arts Tournament; the final starts in manga chapter 128 / Dragon Ball episode 97

beaten.how: In their first fight King Piccolo overpowered young Goku and left him for dead. Goku came back stronger and won the rematch.
beaten.where: King Piccolo Saga; Dragon Ball episode 109

beaten.how: Beerus knocked Goku out with two blows on King Kai's planet. Later, even as a Super Saiyan God, Goku lost the Battle of Gods, though Beerus chose to spare Earth.
beaten.where: God of Destruction Beerus Saga; Dragon Ball Super episodes 5 and 14 (also the film Battle of Gods)

beaten.how: Their fight reached a stalemate, then Goku jumped out of the ring because he had hit the limit of his Kaio-ken, so he lost on a technicality. Hit later threw his next match.
beaten.where: Universe 6 Saga; Dragon Ball Super episode 40

beaten.how: Even with Mastered Ultra Instinct, Goku could not beat Jiren alone. Goku and Frieza finally pushed Jiren out together in a triple elimination, and Android 17 won.
beaten.where: Universe Survival Saga (Tournament of Power); Dragon Ball Super episodes 129–131

beaten.how: On New Namek, Moro used magic to drain Goku and Vegeta's life energy until they were close to death.
beaten.where: Galactic Patrol Prisoner Saga (manga only); chapter not confirmed

beaten.how: Granolah beat Goku, whose Ultra Instinct was straining his body and losing accuracy.
beaten.where: Granolah the Survivor Saga (manga only); chapter not confirmed

beaten.how: Frieza came back in his new Black Frieza form and knocked out both Goku and Vegeta with a single blow.
beaten.where: End of the Granolah the Survivor Saga; Dragon Ball Super manga chapter 87

notes: Episode numbers are per series: check 'episodeSeries' (Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z, Dragon Ball Super, GT, Daima). Do not mix them.
Dragon Ball manga chapters use the Japanese continuous numbering (1–519). Viz's 'DBZ' numbering is noted where it differs. Super chapters use the Dragon Ball Super manga's own numbering.
GT and Daima are listed as separate groups. GT is not part of the Super-era continuity. Daima's Super Saiyan 4 is a different version designed by Toriyama.
'Debut' numbers from the Dragon Ball Wiki are when the form or technique first appears on page or screen. For Super Saiyan 2 the form debuts with Gohan, so Goku's numbers are null.

naruto-uzumaki.name: Naruto Uzumaki
naruto-uzumaki.series: Naruto / Naruto Shippuden (Boruto-era forms listed separately)
naruto-uzumaki.summary: Naruto is a ninja who wins through sheer stamina and stubbornness, swamping enemies with clones and finishing them with spinning chakra attacks. As the host of the Nine-Tailed Fox Kurama he has huge chakra reserves, and his strength grows as he learns to work with the fox.

abilities.name: Shadow Clone Technique (Multiple Shadow Clones)
abilities.what: Naruto makes solid copies of himself, often hundreds at once, to outnumber, trick or scout. When a clone disappears, its experience goes back to him, which he also uses to train faster.

abilities.name: Rasengan
abilities.what: A ball of chakra spinning in many directions that grinds into whatever it hits. Naruto first needed a shadow clone to shape it while he supplied the chakra.
abilities.note: These are the numbers for when the technique first appears and Jiraiya starts teaching it. Naruto's first completed Rasengan hits Kabuto in episode 94 (Wikipedia), which the Naruto Wiki cites as chapter 168. Wikipedia's episode list maps episode 94 to chapters 165–167.

abilities.name: Wind Release: Rasenshuriken
abilities.what: Naruto adds his wind chakra to the Rasengan, making a shuriken-shaped blast that cuts his target at the cellular level. It was key to beating Kakuzu, and later he learned to throw it.
abilities.note: Numbers from the Naruto Wiki's debut fields.

abilities.name: Sage Mode (Senjutsu)
abilities.what: Naruto blends natural energy with his own chakra, which strengthens his body and techniques and lets him sense chakra from far away. He has to stay still to gather the energy, so he leaves clones behind to collect it for him.
abilities.note: Episode 156 ('Surpassing the Master') is where Wikipedia's summary says he first masters it. He first uses it in battle in episode 163 ('Explode! Sage Mode'). The manga chapter of his first Sage Mode was not confirmed.

abilities.name: Nine-Tails Chakra Mode / Kurama Mode
abilities.what: Naruto pulls Kurama's chakra into a glowing yellow cloak that boosts his speed and strength and gives him chakra arms and small Tailed Beast Balls. Once he and Kurama became partners, it turned into Kurama Mode and Tailed Beast Mode, a giant fox avatar of chakra.
abilities.note: These numbers are for Nine-Tails Chakra Mode. For Kurama Mode, see the forms list.

abilities.name: Six Paths Sage Mode / Six Paths Senjutsu
abilities.what: Hagoromo, the Sage of the Six Paths, gives Naruto power that lets him fly, sense almost anything and form Truth-Seeking Balls from every nature type. It also makes all his other modes much stronger.

forms.name: Nine-Tails Chakra Cloak: Version 1
forms.arc: Sasuke Recovery Mission (Valley of the End), Part I
forms.what: A bubbling red cloak of Kurama's chakra with one or more tails. It makes him stronger but slowly burns his own body.
forms.note: The Naruto Wiki cites chapters 230–232 for the one-tailed cloak at the Valley of the End. Naruto draws on raw red chakra earlier, without the cloak shape. No single first chapter or episode was confirmed.

forms.name: Nine-Tails Chakra Cloak: Version 2
forms.arc: Tenchi Bridge Reconnaissance Mission (vs. Orochimaru), Part II
forms.what: Starting at four tails, the cloak darkens into a mini-fox body around him and he loses control of himself.
forms.note: Wikipedia's Shippuden season 2 summaries show the Four-Tailed form against Orochimaru around episodes 40–41, and Jiraiya describes an earlier off-screen four-tail incident before that. The Naruto Wiki cites chapter 291 for the 'demon fox cloak'. Exact first numbers were left null.

forms.name: Sage Mode
forms.what: Orange markings around toad-like eyes; natural energy boosts everything he does.

forms.name: Nine-Tails Chakra Mode
forms.arc: Fourth Shinobi World War: Countdown (Island Turtle training)
forms.what: A golden chakra cloak he gets after pulling Kurama's chakra out by force, before the two became partners.
forms.note: Chapter 499 is just before the war (around chapter 515), but Shippuden episode 247 is past the episode 197 cut-off, so it is marked as a spoiler to be safe.

forms.name: Kurama Mode (with Tailed Beast Mode)
forms.what: After Naruto learns Kurama's name and the two become partners, the cloak takes on a haori shape, works without the earlier drawbacks, and lets him form a full Kurama avatar.
forms.note: The chapter comes from the Naruto Wiki. Wikipedia's summaries put the partnership in Shippuden episodes 329–330, but the exact first episode was not confirmed.

forms.name: Six Paths Sage Mode
forms.what: Hagoromo's gift: cross-shaped pupils, flight and Truth-Seeking Balls, plus a stronger Kurama cloak on top.

forms.name: Baryon Mode
forms.what: Naruto and Kurama burn their chakra together, a process the wiki compares to nuclear fusion, for a huge boost that also shortens the opponent's life on contact. It costs Kurama his life.
forms.note: Numbers from the Naruto Wiki only. Wikipedia confirms the combination and its cost.

limits.what: Sage Mode needs stillness. He must stay perfectly still to gather natural energy and it runs out mid-fight, so he leaves clones behind to collect more. It runs out against Pain in Shippuden episode 164 ('Danger! Sage Mode Limit Reached').
Before he controlled it, Kurama's red cloak burned his own body, and every extra tail cost him more control. At four tails he went berserk and once badly wounded Jiraiya.
Before Kurama cooperated, using Nine-Tails Chakra Mode was a tug-of-war over chakra that could have killed him.
Baryon Mode uses up Naruto's and Kurama's life force. Kurama died from it, and Naruto lost all of Kurama's chakra.

beaten.how: Their Rasengan and Chidori clashed at the Valley of the End. Sasuke won but could not bring himself to kill Naruto, and left.
beaten.where: Sasuke Recovery Mission; climax around chapter 232, Naruto episode 134 ('The End of Tears', covering chapters 231–235)

beaten.how: Pain's Preta Path caught Naruto and pinned him down with chakra receivers. Naruto broke free after Minato restored the seal and went on to defeat Pain.
beaten.where: Pain's Assault; Naruto Shippuden episodes 165–166

beaten.how: Their rematch at the Valley of the End ended in a draw. Each lost an arm, and then they made peace.
beaten.where: Kaguya Ōtsutsuki Strikes arc; begins in chapters 692–693 / Shippuden episode 475

beaten.how: They captured Naruto during the Chūnin Exams. Boruto, Sasuke and the Kage rescued him.
beaten.where: Boruto: Naruto the Movie (2015)

beaten.how: After unleashing Isshiki's full Kāma power, Jigen beat both Naruto and Sasuke and sealed Naruto away. The strain forced Jigen to withdraw.
beaten.where: Boruto: Kawaki arc; Boruto manga chapter 38, anime episode 204 (covers chapters 37–39)

beaten.how: To keep Naruto out of his war on the Ōtsutsuki, Kawaki sent Naruto and Hinata into Daikokuten, a dimension where time stands still.
beaten.where: End of Boruto: Naruto Next Generations; manga chapter 77

notes: firstEpisode for Part I items uses Naruto (2002) numbering. Items marked episodeSeries 'Naruto Shippuden' use Shippuden numbering, and Baryon Mode uses Boruto anime numbering.
Spoiler cut-off: Fourth Great Ninja War onward (about chapter 515 / Shippuden episode 197), plus all Boruto material.
For abilities, the numbers mean when the technique first appears. Where Naruto's own first use differs (Rasengan), that is stated in 'note'.

luffy-monkey-d.name: Monkey D. Luffy
luffy-monkey-d.summary: Luffy ate the Gum-Gum Fruit as a child, so his whole body stretches like rubber. He fights by turning that rubber body into weapons, then stacking power-ups on top of it: his numbered Gears and, after the two-year timeskip, all three types of Haki.

abilities.name: Gum-Gum Fruit: rubber body
abilities.what: His body is rubber. He can stretch, bounce, twist and inflate any part of himself, shrug off blunt hits and bullets (he bounces them back) and is immune to lightning.
abilities.note: Numbers mark where he eats the fruit (the anime shows it in a flashback in episode 4). Its true name is revealed much later (see Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika).

abilities.name: Gum-Gum techniques
abilities.what: His basic moves stretch a limb back and snap it forward: the Pistol punch, the rapid-fire Gatling, the two-handed Bazooka, the sweeping Whip kick and many more, mostly named after firearms.
abilities.note: The Pistol is used in chapter 1. The wiki pairs that scene with episode 504's retelling, so no single first anime episode is given.

abilities.name: Conqueror's Haki (Supreme King Haki)
abilities.what: A rare Haki that only people with a 'king's' quality have. Luffy's willpower knocks weaker people and animals unconscious. Before the timeskip it bursts out by accident, for example at Amazon Lily and at Marineford.
abilities.note: Numbers are the wiki's first unintentional use (stopping a bison on Sabaody). Better-known early uses: chapter 519 / episode 413 (Amazon Lily) and chapter 569 / episode 478 (Marineford).

abilities.name: Armament Haki
abilities.what: Learned from Rayleigh during the two-year timeskip. It hardens his limbs black, adding power and defense, and lets him hit Logia users like Caesar Clown who would otherwise turn intangible.
abilities.note: No first post-timeskip use was confirmed, so the numbers are left null.

abilities.name: Observation Haki
abilities.what: Also learned during the timeskip. It lets him sense people's presence, emotions and intentions, so he can dodge bullets and attacks before they land.

abilities.name: Future Sight (advanced Observation Haki)
abilities.what: Pushed to his limit by Katakuri, Luffy learns to see a few seconds into the future. In Wano he can read the short-term future as smoothly as Katakuri.

abilities.name: Advanced Armament Haki (Emission and Internal Destruction)
abilities.what: Trained by Hyougoro in Udon prison, he learns to project Haki a short distance without touching the target, and to send it inside a target to destroy it from within. This is how he finally hurts Kaidou.
abilities.note: Numbers are his first Internal Destruction. Wikipedia names both applications.

abilities.name: Conqueror's Haki coating (advanced Conqueror's Haki)
abilities.what: During the Kaidou fight he learns to wrap his fists in Conqueror's Haki, shown by black lightning. Only a handful of top fighters can do this. His clashes with Kaidou split the sky.

abilities.name: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika
abilities.what: The Gum-Gum Fruit's real identity: a Mythical Zoan fruit that turns him into the sun god Nika, the 'Warrior of Liberation'. Its awakening (Gear 5) makes his rubber body almost limitless. Luffy himself does not know this yet.

forms.name: Gear 2
forms.what: He pumps blood through his body at high speed, like doping. His rubber blood vessels survive the pressure, so he becomes far faster and hits harder, giving off steam while it lasts.
forms.note: Debut numbers are from the One Piece Wiki infobox (first used against Blueno).

forms.name: Gear 3
forms.what: He bites his thumb and blows air into his bones, inflating a limb to giant size for huge, slow, crushing blows.
forms.note: Chapter 403 / episode 288 is the first (off-panel) use on a steel door. It is first fully shown in chapter 421 / episode 304 against Rob Lucci.

forms.name: Nightmare Luffy
forms.what: A one-off power-up: 100 stolen shadows are packed into Luffy, making him huge, blue and much stronger for about ten minutes. One shadow even lets him use a sword.
forms.note: One-time situational form, not a Gear. Only the One Piece Wiki was checked for the numbers.

forms.name: Gear 4: Boundman
forms.what: He inflates his muscles, coats his body in Armament Haki and becomes a bouncing rubber ball. He compresses his limbs into his body and fires them out with huge force, and can fly by bouncing off the air.
forms.note: He starts activating it at the end of chapter 783 / episode 725. Gear 4 was developed during the two-year timeskip.

forms.name: Gear 4: Tankman
forms.what: A huge, round, defensive Gear 4 shape. Attacks bounce off him and their recoil is thrown back at the attacker. It has only been seen in its 'full stomach' version after he ate a mountain of Cracker's biscuits.

forms.name: Gear 4: Snakeman
forms.what: A slimmer, speed-focused Gear 4. His punches keep accelerating and can change direction mid-flight to chase the target, at the cost of less defense.
forms.note: Numbers are where he first names Snakeman against Katakuri. The form's power is explained in chapter 895 / episode 870.

forms.name: Gear 5
forms.what: After his Devil Fruit awakens, Luffy turns white and fights like a cartoon: he can reshape his body however he imagines and even turn the ground, objects and people around him into rubber. He calls it the peak of his power.
forms.note: Also appears in One Piece Film: Red, but chapter 1044 / episode 1071 is the canon debut.

limits.what: Like every Devil Fruit user he cannot swim. Seawater and Seastone drain his strength, and Seastone cuffs stop his powers entirely.
Rubber only protects him from blunt force. Blades and cutting attacks hurt him normally, and shockwave attacks such as Fish-Man Karate get through too.
Gear 2 burns huge amounts of energy, leaving him starving or barely able to move, and Rob Lucci warns it can shorten his life.
Before the timeskip, Gear 3 shrank him to a tiny, weak size for a while after each use.
When Gear 4 runs out he is drained and cannot use Haki for about ten minutes, On Whole Cake Island, while his Haki recharged, even Gear 3 could not break through Perospero's candy wall.

Gear 5 uses up his stamina fast. When it ends he looks like a shriveled old man until he eats or rests, and its changes to the world are temporary. As an awakened Zoan it also carries a risk of Nika's nature taking over his mind, and he is still vulnerable to cuts.

beaten.how: In their first fight in the desert, Crocodile's sand powers dried out Luffy's arm and he was left in quicksand for dead. Luffy only beat him in their third fight.
beaten.where: Alabasta Arc; first fight chapters 177–178, episodes 110–111

beaten.how: Luffy fought the Admiral one-on-one and was frozen solid. Aokiji left without killing him and the crew thawed him out.
beaten.where: Long Ring Long Land Arc; chapter 321, episode 228

beaten.how: Luffy hit Kaidou with Gear 3 and Gear 4 but was knocked out with a single blow and thrown in prison. Kaidou downed him again during the Onigashima raid before Luffy awakened Gear 5 and finally beat him.
beaten.where: Wano Country Arc; first loss chapter 923, episode 915; Luffy's win chapter 1049, episode 1076

notes: Episode numbers are the One Piece TV anime's running numbers. Chapter numbers are the One Piece manga.
Debut numbers come from the One Piece Wiki's infobox and citation fields. Wikipedia confirms each form and Haki type exists but does not give numbers.
Spoiler cut-off: after Marineford (chapter 597 / episode 516). That is why Armament and Observation Haki are marked as spoilers: Luffy learns them in the two-year timeskip.
No new Gear beyond Gear 5 was found in the sources checked. Gear 5 moves like Gomu Gomu no Majin are techniques, not new forms.
luffy-monkey-d.hook: All Gears in order (2 to 5), Haki & Nika
luffy-monkey-d.powersLine: his Gears (Gear 2, Gear 3, the three Gear 4 forms and Gear 5), his rubber body from the Gum-Gum Fruit, and all three types of Haki

jujutsu-kaisen-sukuna.name: Ryomen Sukuna
jujutsu-kaisen-sukuna.summary: Sukuna is the King of Curses, a sorcerer from the Heian era so strong that his soul survived death split across twenty cursed fingers. When Yuji Itadori eats one, Sukuna wakes up inside him. His power is built on invisible slashes, a fire arrow, a domain that cuts everything around him, and very fast healing.

abilities.name: Shrine: Dismantle
abilities.what: Sukuna's main cursed technique. Dismantle is an invisible slash that flies at the target, usually aimed with a point of the finger. How deep it cuts depends on how much cursed energy he puts in.
abilities.note: The numbers are the wiki's debut for Shrine as a whole. Dismantle and Cleave are first named and explained in the Shibuya arc (chapter 119 / episode 41).

abilities.name: Shrine: Cleave
abilities.what: A slash that adjusts its strength to the target's toughness and cursed energy, so it cuts them apart in one hit. Outside his domain Sukuna has to touch the target to use it.
abilities.note: Same debut note as Dismantle. The touch requirement is stated in chapter 246.

abilities.name: Domain Expansion: Malevolent Shrine
abilities.what: His domain summons a shrine decorated with skulls. Instead of closing the space with a barrier, it covers the surrounding area, and everything inside is shredded nonstop by Dismantle and Cleave. Leaving an escape route works like a binding vow that hugely enlarges its range.
abilities.note: Debut numbers are from the wiki, where the shrine first appears. Its first full use in a big fight comes later in the story (Wikipedia, season 2).

abilities.name: Reverse Cursed Technique
abilities.what: He turns cursed energy into positive energy to heal instantly, even regrowing Yuji's severed hand in moments. Unusually, he can also heal other people.

abilities.name: Divine Flame (fire arrow, 'Fuga' / 'Open')
abilities.what: After using Dismantle and Cleave, he says 'Open', shapes fire into an arrow and fires it. Its flames overpower Jogo, a special-grade curse made of fire. The technique's real name, Divine Flame, is only revealed much later.
abilities.note: First used against Jogo in chapters 115–116, episode 40. The name 'Divine Flame' is first given in chapter 258–259.

abilities.name: Ten Shadows Technique and Mahoraga
abilities.what: After taking Megumi's body he can use Megumi's shikigami, which are stronger in his hands. That includes Mahoraga, which Sukuna had defeated in Shibuya. He uses Mahoraga's ability to adapt to anything against Gojo, and copies its adaptation to learn a slash that can cut through Gojo's Infinity.
abilities.note: Number is where Sukuna summons Mahoraga against Gojo. He first fights Mahoraga, summoned by Megumi, in chapters 118–119 / episode 41.

abilities.name: World-cutting slash
abilities.what: Using Mahoraga's adaptation as a model, he upgrades Dismantle so it cuts space itself. This is how he gets past Gojo's Infinity.
abilities.note: Manga only.

forms.name: Sukuna in Yuji's body
forms.what: Sukuna's usual state for most of the story. When he takes over, Yuji's body grows Sukuna's tattoos and a second pair of eyes. Sukuna can also open a mouth or eye on Yuji's cheek to talk while Yuji is in control.
forms.note: Numbers are when Yuji eats the first finger.

forms.name: Sukuna in Megumi's body
forms.what: Sukuna turns one of Yuji's fingers into a cursed object, forces Megumi to swallow it and moves into Megumi's body. This gives him Megumi's Ten Shadows Technique.
forms.note: Manga only. No anime episode was found in any source checked.

forms.name: Sukuna's true form
forms.what: His original Heian-era body: four arms, four eyes and a second mouth on his stomach. The extra arms let him make hand signs while still fighting, and the second mouth can chant without tiring him.
forms.note: The transformation happens in chapter 237. The wiki explains the body's advantages in chapter 238. Manga only.

limits.what: For most of the story he is stuck inside Yuji and rarely in control. His 'Enchain' deal gives him only one minute in charge, and Yuji made him promise not to hurt anyone during it.
His strength depends on how many fingers he has eaten. With only a few, he is far below his full power.
After losing a hand, he needed a binding vow to keep using the world-cutting slash: each use now needs the hand sign, the spoken incantation and aiming with his palm.
Divine Flame is slow and narrow, so he swore a binding vow not to use it when outnumbered unless he is inside his domain. In return, his domain turns into a giant explosion when he fires it.

beaten.who: Yuji Itadori (with Nobara, Megumi and the other sorcerers)
beaten.how: Sukuna killed Gojo, but the remaining sorcerers kept fighting him in relays. Yuji trapped him in his own domain. Nobara's Resonance on the last finger broke Sukuna's domain, and Megumi's soul resisted from inside. Yuji's final punch tore Megumi free, and Sukuna refused Yuji's offer to live with him and disintegrated.
beaten.where: Shinjuku Showdown Arc; manga chapter 268

notes: Anime episode numbers are series-wide: season 2 episode 1 = episode 25, so episode 41 = season 2 episode 17.
Chapter numbers are the main Jujutsu Kaisen manga.
Spoiler cut-off: the Shibuya Incident onward (chapter 83 / episode 30).
Culling Game and Shinjuku material from chapter 212 on is marked manga only: no source checked gives an anime episode, so firstEpisode is null.
In the Heian era Sukuna was never defeated. His only loss is the Shinjuku battle.
jujutsu-kaisen-sukuna.hook: Shrine, Malevolent Shrine & the fire arrow
jujutsu-kaisen-sukuna.powersLine: his cursed technique Shrine (Dismantle and Cleave), the fire arrow, his Domain Expansion Malevolent Shrine, and Reverse Cursed Technique

sung-jin-woo.name: Sung Jin-Woo
sung-jin-woo.summary: Jin-Woo starts as the weakest E-rank hunter. After nearly dying in the Double Dungeon he becomes the 'Player' of a mysterious System that lets him level up like a video game character. His job change turns him into a necromancer-type class who raises defeated enemies as a loyal shadow army.

abilities.name: The System (Player)
abilities.what: A game-like screen only he can see. It gives him daily quests, levels, stat points, skills, rewards, an inventory and a shop, and sends him to a penalty zone if he skips a daily quest.
abilities.note: In the anime the 'Player' offer arrives at the end of episode 2 and he sees the System properly in episode 3.

abilities.name: Shadow Extraction ('Arise')
abilities.what: He can pull the shadow out of a defeated enemy's body and raise it as a loyal shadow soldier. It costs no mana and works over a wide area, so he can raise many soldiers at once.
abilities.note: Gained as the reward for the job-change quest. Wikipedia's episode 12 summary says the anime calls the new title 'Shadow Monarch'.

abilities.name: Shadow army
abilities.what: His raised soldiers keep their skills and fight for him. Key soldiers include Igris (the knight from his job-change quest), Iron, Tusk, Kaisel (Baran's dragon) and Beru (the Ant King), who can talk.
abilities.note: Igris: chapter 45 / episode 12. Beru: chapter 105 / episode 25. Iron, Tusk and Kaisel are raised in episodes 14, 18 and 20.

abilities.name: Shadow Preservation (Shadow Storage)
abilities.what: He keeps his shadow soldiers stored inside his own shadow and can summon or recall them at will. At a higher level he can also see and hear through them.
abilities.note: Only the Solo Leveling Wiki gives this skill's debut.

abilities.name: Shadow Exchange
abilities.what: He swaps places with any of his shadow soldiers, no matter how far away. He gets it for beating Demon King Baran and uses it to join the Jeju Island fight.
abilities.note: Episode number is from Wikipedia's episode 20 summary. The wiki gives only the webtoon chapter.

abilities.name: Ruler's Hand
abilities.what: A telekinesis skill from the rune stone he gets for beating Igris. He uses it to move objects and pull back his thrown dagger.
abilities.note: The wiki lists chapter 40 / episode 12 as the debut.

abilities.name: Ruler's Authority
abilities.what: Ruler's Hand evolves into a full-strength telekinesis that can pin many enemies at once, push off the air to fly and dodge, and work against Monarch-level foes.
abilities.note: Evolves during his fight with Kandiaru's statues in the Double Dungeon (webtoon chapter 126). No anime episode yet.

abilities.name: Bloodlust (Murderous Intent)
abilities.what: He frightens targets into freezing in place and halves their stats for a short time. It works on several enemies at once. He first gets it as a reward for the System quest to kill Hwang Dongsuk's group.
abilities.note: The anime calls it Murderous Intent.

abilities.name: Quicksilver (Sprint / Dash)
abilities.what: A speed boost that starts at +30% and grows as the skill levels up.

abilities.name: Mutilation (Critical Attack / Fatal Strike)
abilities.what: A dagger skill that targets vital points. Its evolved form rips an enemy apart with a rapid chain of slashes.

abilities.name: Dagger Rush (Dagger Throw)
abilities.what: He throws daggers with high accuracy. The evolved version hits the target with daggers from every direction.

abilities.name: Stealth
abilities.what: He hides his body and presence, becoming physically and magically invisible. It drains mana quickly.
abilities.note: The numbers are the skill's debut, when Kang Taeshik uses it on Jin-Woo's group. Jin-Woo uses it after that.

abilities.name: Monarch's Domain
abilities.what: His shadow spreads over the battlefield and makes all his shadow soldiers 50% stronger.
abilities.note: Only the webtoon chapter is listed. No anime episode is cited.

abilities.name: Dragon's Fear
abilities.what: A mana-filled roar that throws everyone weaker than him into panic and despair.
abilities.note: The wiki gives only a web novel chapter (173), so the webtoon chapter is left null.

abilities.name: Shadow Monarch's true power
abilities.what: He learns he was chosen as the successor of Ashborn, the original Shadow Monarch, and inherits his full power: he stops aging, gains near-unlimited mana and total control of shadows, and Shadow Exchange loses its limits so he can teleport anywhere.
abilities.note: ComicBook places his meeting with Ashborn in webtoon chapter 162 and his return in chapter 164. The wiki puts the upgraded Shadow Exchange at chapter 165. No single first chapter is given here.

limits.what: Skipping the System's daily quest sends him to a deadly penalty zone. He nearly dies the first time.
Shadow Extraction can fail. The odds depend on how strong the target is and how long it has been dead, he gets only three tries per corpse, and targets much stronger than him cannot be raised.
Shadow Extraction cannot raise Rulers or Monarchs, whose bodies are made of mana.
Stealth can be seen through by mages and monsters with detection skills. In the anime, mages break his Stealth in episode 11.
At first, Shadow Exchange only worked if a shadow soldier was already at the destination, and it had a three-hour cooldown.
Dragon's Fear hits everyone weaker than him nearby, allies included, and does nothing to stronger enemies.

beaten.who: The statues of the Double Dungeon (Statue of God)
beaten.how: Already missing a leg, Jin-Woo stayed behind so the others could escape and was skewered by the statues. As he was dying, the System offered him the chance to become a Player and he accepted.
beaten.where: Double Dungeon; webtoon chapter 10, anime episode 2

beaten.how: While Jin-Woo was fighting Sillad, Rakan struck him from behind with a fatal blow. Inside, Jin-Woo met Ashborn, came back with the Shadow Monarch's full power and defeated both of them.
beaten.where: Monarchs War Arc; fatal blow in webtoon chapter 161, return in chapter 164

notes: Chapter numbers are the Solo Leveling webtoon (KakaoPage / Webtoon). Web novel numbers are different and are only mentioned in notes.
Episode numbers run across seasons: season 1 is episodes 1–12 and season 2 (Arise from the Shadow) is episodes 13–25.
Spoiler cut-off: anything after season 2 ends (webtoon chapter 110), plus everything about what being the 'Shadow Monarch' really means (Ashborn, Rulers, Monarchs).
Most debut numbers come only from the Solo Leveling Wiki's skill infoboxes. Wikipedia's episode summaries confirm System, Shadow Extraction, the soldiers, Shadow Exchange and Bloodlust.
No sourced transformations, so forms is empty.
sung-jin-woo.hook: The System, Shadow Extraction & the shadow army
sung-jin-woo.powersLine: the System that levels him up, Shadow Extraction ('Arise') and his shadow army, Shadow Exchange, Ruler's Hand, and his dagger skills

itachi-uchiha.name: Itachi Uchiha
itachi-uchiha.summary: Itachi is an Uchiha prodigy and Sasuke's older brother, known as the man who wiped out his own clan and joined the Akatsuki. He is one of the series' best genjutsu users. His Mangekyō Sharingan gives him a mind-breaking illusion, black flames that will not go out, and a giant spectral guardian, but every use costs him his eyesight.

abilities.name: Sharingan
abilities.what: He awakened the Sharingan at age 8. It lets him see chakra, read and predict movements, and cast genjutsu with a look. He can even turn an enemy's genjutsu back on them.
abilities.note: Numbers are the debut of the genjutsu he reflects back at Kurenai in his first fight in Konoha. Wikipedia's episode 82 summary describes his Sharingan duel with Kakashi.

abilities.name: Genjutsu
abilities.what: His specialty. His illusions are strong even without the Sharingan, can be cast just by pointing, and often use crows. He uses them to pass on information or to end a fight instantly.
abilities.note: Same debut as the Sharingan entry.

abilities.name: Mangekyō Sharingan
abilities.what: His advanced Sharingan, awakened after Shisui's death, with a three-curve pattern. It unlocks Tsukuyomi, Amaterasu and, with both eyes, Susanoo.
abilities.note: The full story of how he awakened it is part of the later reveals about Itachi.

abilities.name: Tsukuyomi
abilities.what: A Mangekyō genjutsu that traps the victim in a world Itachi controls, where days of torture can pass in an instant. It can break the mind badly enough to put strong ninja in the hospital.
abilities.note: Used on Kakashi in episode 82 and on Sasuke in episodes 84–85.

abilities.name: Amaterasu
abilities.what: Black flames that ignite wherever he looks, using his right eye. They burn even through other fire and do not go out until he lets them.
abilities.note: Numbers are the wiki's debut, in his Part I clash with Jiraiya. Wikipedia's Shippuden episode 137 summary shows him using it on Sasuke.

abilities.name: Susanoo
abilities.what: Using both Mangekyō eyes, he summons a giant spectral warrior around himself that blocks almost any attack. Even partial versions give him extra arms or ribs for defense.
abilities.note: Revealed in his fight with Sasuke. Episode 138 is Naruto Shippuden numbering.

abilities.name: Sword of Totsuka
abilities.what: The ethereal sword of Itachi's Susanoo. Anyone it pierces is sealed inside the gourd at its hilt.

abilities.name: Yata Mirror
abilities.what: The shield of Itachi's Susanoo. It is said to bounce back any attack by changing its chakra nature to cancel it out. With the sword and shield together, his Susanoo is described as almost invincible.

abilities.name: Shadow Clone Explosion
abilities.what: He makes shadow clones that blow up, using them as decoys that explode in the enemy's face.
abilities.note: The English anime calls it Shadow Clone Explosion. The wiki's name is Clone Great Explosion.

abilities.name: Crow Clone and crows
abilities.what: He summons flocks of crows to distract and blind opponents, and builds crows into clones of himself.
abilities.note: Episode 14 is Naruto Shippuden numbering.

abilities.name: Fire Release
abilities.what: As an Uchiha he is a master of fire. He learned the clan's Great Fireball Technique very young and coats shuriken in flames. He can also use Water Release without a nearby water source.
abilities.note: No first chapter or episode was confirmed.

abilities.name: Amaterasu sealed in Sasuke's eye
abilities.what: Before dying, Itachi poked Sasuke's forehead and sealed Amaterasu into his eye, set to fire automatically if Tobi's Sharingan ever met it.
abilities.note: Chapter 397 is where the seal is explained (wiki). Wikipedia's Shippuden episode 139 summary shows the flames bursting from Sasuke's eye at Tobi.

abilities.name: Izanami
abilities.what: An Uchiha genjutsu that traps the target in an endless loop of the same moments. The only way out is to stop fighting fate and accept who you are. Itachi uses it on Kabuto to make him end the Impure World Reincarnation.
abilities.note: Fourth Great Ninja War, so it is a spoiler.

limits.what: Every use of the Mangekyō Sharingan worsens his eyesight. At first his eyes only bled, but by his fight with Sasuke he can barely see. He tells Sasuke the only cure is to take a sibling's eyes.
The Mangekyō uses a huge amount of chakra. Three uses in one day left him unable to use even the normal Sharingan until he had rested a long time.

He was secretly dying of an incurable illness, kept alive by medicine and willpower so he could last until Sasuke came for him. That is why he avoided long fights. After he was brought back by Impure World Reincarnation, his illness and eye damage were gone.
Izanami always leaves an escape route: the victim gets out by accepting their fate. Itachi chose to give Kabuto that chance.

beaten.how: Their fight seems to end in Sasuke's favour. Itachi survives Kirin with Susanoo and seals away Orochimaru, but then, coughing blood and with Sasuke helpless in front of him, he only pokes Sasuke's forehead and collapses dead. The series later reveals he was already dying of illness and had planned the fight to free Sasuke from Orochimaru and make him a hero.
beaten.where: Fated Battle Between Brothers; manga chapter 393, Naruto Shippuden episode 138

notes: Episode numbers use the 'episodeSeries' field: Naruto (2002) for Part I, Naruto Shippuden for Part II. Do not mix them.

Spoiler cut-off: the Fourth Great Ninja War (about chapter 515 / Shippuden episode 197) and the truth behind Itachi (chapter 399 onward). His illness, his real plan for the Sasuke fight and his later reveals are all marked as spoilers.

Ability numbers are the Naruto Wiki's 'debut manga' and 'debut anime' fields. For Tsukuyomi, Amaterasu, Susanoo, Totsuka, Yata, Shadow Clone Explosion and Izanami, Itachi is the first person to use the technique.
In the main story, the Sasuke fight is the only time Itachi 'loses', and the series presents it as a loss he chose.
itachi-uchiha.powersLine: his Sharingan and genjutsu, the Mangekyō Sharingan (Tsukuyomi, Amaterasu and Susanoo with the Sword of Totsuka and Yata Mirror), Shadow Clone Explosion and Izanami
